nodes.label: mtLoRA: Spectral Multitask Regularization for LoRA

attributes.key_contribution: Three novel LoRA designs: spectral-aware regularization, fine-grained routing, block-level adaptation. Achieves 64.0% avg vs HydraLoRA 61.7% with 47% fewer parameters.

nodes.label: RMT Analysis of Feature Learning in Two-Layer NNs (Spiked SRFM)

attributes.key_contribution: Proves spiked SRFM approximation W^1 = W^0 + uv^T + Delta. Derives deterministic equivalent for feature covariance. Proves exact generalization error formula (Theorem 4.8). Feature learning creates heavier tails → better generalization.

nodes.label: SANE: Scalable and Versatile Weight Space Learning

attributes.key_contribution: Sequential Autoencoder for Neural Embeddings. Tokenizes weights layer-wise into windows. Scales to ResNet-18 (~12M params). Outperforms hyper-representations by 25% for zero-shot initialization.

nodes.label: Subspace-Boosted Model Merging via HO-GSVD

attributes.key_contribution: Identifies rank collapse: task-specific SVs decay O(1/sqrt(N)). Proposes Subspace Boosting (clamp small SVs above beta threshold). Introduces HO-GSVD alignment matrix for task similarity.

nodes.label: Gradient Space LoRA: Task Discovery via SVD

attributes.key_contribution: Analyzes gradient space of LoRA through SVD lens to discover task-relevant directions. Links gradient space structure to task residual spectrum.

nodes.label: Heavy-Tailed Mechanistic Universality (HTMP)

attributes.key_contribution: HTMP as improved null distribution over standard Marchenko-Pastur for weight matrices. Heavy-tailed correction accounts for non-Gaussian weight statistics in real neural networks.

nodes.label: Deep Synthesis Night Run 1: Hidden Geometry of Weight Space

attributes.key_contribution: Identifies TRS theory as incomplete; proposes eight frameworks: four-way decomposition, fiber bundle, spectral-population duality, knowledge region as TRS manifold, weight disentanglement = TRS orthogonality, near-zero SVs as anti-tasks, model stitching as TRS test, TRS as sufficient statistic, platonic weight space hypothesis.

nodes.label: New Papers Found: Night Run May 2026

attributes.key_contribution: Catalog of 16 new papers supporting and extending TRS theory across 8 thematic categories.

nodes.label: Four-Way Spectral Decomposition of LoRA

attributes.description: The singular value spectrum of DeltaW decomposes into four functionally distinct regions: (1) True TRS (above-MP, aligned with pre-trained SVs = task signal), (2) Intruder Dimensions (above-MP, NOT aligned = catastrophic forgetting), (3) MP Bulk (within Marchenko-Pastur = domain adaptation), (4) Near-Zero Suppression (below lower MP threshold = capability suppression, not noise).
attributes.formal: TRS_refined(B) = {u_i : sigma_i > sigma_MP_upper AND cos(u_i, V_pretrained) > tau_align}
attributes.rationale: Extends existing TRS framework which only distinguished above-MP vs below-MP. Incorporating alignment criterion separates task signal from forgetting artifacts.

nodes.label: True TRS (Task Residual Spectrum, Refined)

attributes.description: Singular vectors above Marchenko-Pastur upper bound AND aligned with pre-trained singular vectors. Represents genuine task acquisition signal. Predicts task-specific performance improvement.
attributes.formal: TRS_+ = {u_i : sigma_i > sigma_MP_upper AND cos(u_i, V_pretrained) > tau_align}
attributes.rationale: Distinguishes true task signal from intruder dimensions by adding the alignment criterion to the above-MP condition.

nodes.label: Intruder Dimensions

attributes.description: High-magnitude singular vectors in fine-tuned LoRA that are DISSIMILAR to pre-trained singular vectors. Concentrate catastrophic forgetting artifacts. Suppressing them largely restores base model knowledge.
attributes.formal: intruder_score(LoRA) = ||{sigma_i above-MP, not aligned with V_pretrained}||
attributes.rationale: Current TRS includes intruder dimensions by mistake; they predict forgetting, not task performance.

nodes.label: Marchenko-Pastur Bulk (MP Bulk)

attributes.description: Singular values within the Marchenko-Pastur distribution. Encodes domain adaptation / common subspace information. Preserved by averaging (proved by Subspace-Boosted Merging). Not task-specific but not pure noise either.
attributes.rationale: MP bulk is the third region of the four-way decomposition; it carries distribution-level information rather than task-specific information.

nodes.label: Near-Zero Singular Values as Anti-Tasks (TRS_-)

attributes.description: Singular vectors below the lower MP threshold. NOT noise — structured capability suppression. Removing them causes outsized performance collapse. Fine-tuning deliberately suppresses certain capabilities to specialize.
attributes.formal: TRS_- = {singular vectors with sigma < sigma_MP_lower, sigma > 0} = capabilities SUPPRESSED
attributes.application: Forgetting diagnosis: if TRS_-(T1) intersect TRS_+(T2) != empty, then training on T1 will catastrophically forget T2.
attributes.rationale: Fourth region of decomposition; capability suppression creates the specialization signature of fine-tuning.

nodes.label: Rank Collapse in Model Merging

attributes.description: When merging N task vectors via Task Arithmetic, task-specific singular values decay O(1/sqrt(N)) while common subspace SVs remain O(1). Stable rank collapses to stable rank of common subspace only.
propositions: Prop 2: stable rank collapses to common subspace stable rank
attributes.rationale: Explains why naive averaging destroys task-specific information and motivates subspace boosting.

nodes.label: Subspace Boosting Algorithm

attributes.description: SVD-based mitigation of rank collapse. Clamps small singular values above a beta threshold to preserve task-specific subspace structure during model merging.
attributes.pseudocode: U, S, Vh = svd(param); c_sum = torch.cumsum(S); k = (n_sum >= beta).nonzero(); S_new = torch.clamp(S, S[idx]); new_param = U @ diag(S_new) @ Vh
attributes.rationale: Directly counteracts O(1/sqrt(N)) SV decay by enforcing minimum singular value magnitude.

nodes.label: HO-GSVD (Higher-Order Generalized SVD) for Task Similarity

attributes.description: Decomposes N task vectors into distinct U_i Sigma_i and shared V subspace: A_i = U_i Sigma_i V^T where V is shared. Alignment Matrix A_{ij} = (1/L) sum_l (1/M_l) sum_p |log(sigma^(l)_{i,p} / sigma^(l)_{j,p})| measures task similarity.
attributes.formal: A_i = U_i Sigma_i V^T, V in R^{n x n} shared across all tasks
attributes.rationale: Enables principled comparison of task subspaces across multiple models by factoring out the shared basis.

nodes.label: Spectral-Aware Regularization (mtLoRA)

attributes.description: Selectively orthogonalizes only low-SV components of LoRA matrices across tasks. Uses weight w(sigma) = exp(-sigma/sigma_bar) so that high-SV (shared knowledge) components are preserved while low-SV (task-specific) components are orthogonalized.
attributes.formal: L_spectral = lambda * sum_{i<j} ||(B'_i)^T B'_j||^2_F, where B' is SV-weighted
attributes.empirical_finding: High-SV top-20% components have 89% inter-task alignment; bottom 50% have only 3%.
attributes.rationale: Exploits the empirical observation that high-SV components are shared across tasks while low-SV components are task-specific.

nodes.label: Block-Level Adaptation (mtLoRA)

attributes.description: LoRA as parallel path bypassing attention/FFN non-linearities. Reduces gradient conflict from -0.054 to -0.013 cosine similarity across tasks.
attributes.rationale: Non-linearities introduce gradient conflicts in multitask learning; bypassing them with LoRA parallel paths reduces inter-task interference.

nodes.label: Fine-Grained Routing (mtLoRA)

attributes.description: Dimension-specific MLP router producing weight vectors Pi_i in R^g for g groups. Routes task-specific information to appropriate LoRA dimensions at fine granularity.
attributes.rationale: Coarser task-level routing (e.g., MoE per layer) wastes capacity; dimension-level routing allows more precise task specialization.

nodes.label: Spiked RMT / SRFM (Spiked Random Feature Model)

attributes.description: Weight matrix after one gradient step: W^1 = W^0 + uv^T + Delta, where spike v is correlated with target direction w*. Proved via deterministic equivalent of feature covariance matrix.
attributes.formal: W^1 = W^0 + uv^T + Delta; spike v correlated with w*
attributes.theorem: Theorem 4.8: exact generalization error formula derivable from spiked SRFM approximation
attributes.rationale: Provides theoretical grounding for why feature learning (not just lazy/NTK regime) creates above-MP singular value spikes.

nodes.label: Deterministic Equivalent for Feature Covariance

attributes.description: RMT technique that replaces stochastic feature covariance matrix with a deterministic approximation that captures the same spectral statistics. Used to prove exact generalization error in the spiked SRFM setting.
attributes.rationale: Enables rigorous theoretical analysis of feature learning without requiring independence assumptions that fail in practice.

nodes.label: Hyper-Representations via SANE

attributes.description: Task-agnostic latent space embeddings of neural network weights. SANE encodes weight sequences into embeddings that correlate with WeightWatcher metrics and model accuracy. Scales 3 orders of magnitude beyond previous hyper-representation methods.
attributes.rationale: Task-agnostic training enables generalization across model architectures and tasks; sequential tokenization preserves layer-wise structure.

nodes.label: Weight Tokenization (SANE)

attributes.description: Tokenizes NN weight sequences into windows of size ws. Each token = weight window from a layer. Enables transformer encoder to process weights of arbitrary architectures sequentially.
attributes.formal: Input: weight matrices M_{s,n}, tokenized into windows; Loss: L_rec = ||M_{s,n} odot (T_{s,n} - T_hat_{s,n})||^2 + L_c (NTXent contrastive)
attributes.rationale: Fixed-window tokenization allows SANE to handle variable-size networks without architecture-specific preprocessing.

nodes.label: Fiber Bundle Framework for Weight Space

attributes.description: Neural network weight space W as a fiber bundle. Total space W = R^d. Base space T = task manifold (parameterized by TRS_refined directions). Fiber F_w = {w' : TRS_refined(w') = TRS_refined(w)} = G-symmetry equivalence class. Projection pi(w) = TRS_refined(w). Structure group G = permutation symmetry group.
attributes.connection: Connection 1-form = Fisher Information Matrix restricted to task directions.
attributes.explanatory_power: Weight alignment NP-hard = different sections of fiber bundle; task arithmetic works = addition in base space T; merging fails = holonomy; mode connectivity = paths in T lifting to W.
attributes.rationale: Provides a unified geometric framework that explains all existing model composition methods as special cases.

nodes.label: Holonomy as Task Interference

attributes.description: Curvature of the fiber bundle connection encodes interference between tasks. If two task vectors tau_1, tau_2 have non-zero holonomy, then task arithmetic fails for them. This is precisely the disentanglement error xi(alpha_1, alpha_2) from Ortiz-Jiménez et al.
attributes.formal: Non-zero holonomy(tau_1, tau_2) <=> task arithmetic fails for (tau_1, tau_2)
attributes.rationale: Holonomy formalizes why task composition sometimes fails: going around a loop in task manifold T doesn't return to same fiber point.

nodes.label: Weight Disentanglement = TRS Orthogonality

attributes.description: Two task vectors tau_1, tau_2 are weight-disentangled iff their TRS_refined subspaces are orthogonal in the Grassmannian sense: d_Grassmannian(TRS_refined(tau_1), TRS_refined(tau_2)) ≈ 1 (= pi/2 principal angle).
attributes.prediction: For random init models: d_Grassmannian non-orthogonal. For pre-trained models: d_Grassmannian ≈ 1. Matches empirical finding that task arithmetic is emergent property of pre-training.
attributes.rationale: Pre-training induces NTK eigenfunctions that localize to task domains, producing nearly orthogonal TRS directions for different tasks.

nodes.label: Spectral-Population Duality

attributes.description: The k-th principal component of population-level PCA = linear combination of TRS vectors across individual LoRAs: PC_k = sum_i alpha_{ik} * TRS_i(B_i). w2w space = space spanned by TRS vectors across population. Hyper-representations = encodings converging to TRS-based features.
attributes.prediction: Cosine similarity between PC_k of w2w and average TRS_k across models should be r > 0.7.
attributes.rationale: PCA on a population of LoRAs is an efficient approximation of TRS; this explains WHY population-level PCA works.

nodes.label: Platonic Weight Space Hypothesis

attributes.description: As models scale, weight space structure converges to a canonical form. NTK eigenfunctions become increasingly localized. Spectral structure approaches universal Marchenko-Pastur + task spikes form. TRS directions for same task become increasingly aligned across architectures.
attributes.prediction: For larger models (GPT-4, Llama-3-70B), TRS cross-architecture alignment higher than for smaller models (Llama-3-8B, Mistral-7B).
attributes.analogy: Weight-space analog of Platonic Representation Hypothesis (Huh et al., ICML 2024).
attributes.rationale: Scale drives convergence of representational geometry; this should manifest in weight space as well as activation space.

nodes.label: Marchenko-Pastur Distribution

attributes.description: Standard null hypothesis for random weight matrices. Describes the expected singular value distribution of a random Gaussian matrix. Deviations above upper bound = signal; deviations below lower bound = suppression (not noise per Staats et al.).
attributes.rationale: Provides the null against which task-relevant spectral deviations are measured.

nodes.label: Grassmannian Distance for Subspace Comparison

attributes.description: Proper metric for comparing task subspaces via principal angles between subspaces, not cosine similarity of individual vectors. Critical for cross-architecture TRS comparison and weight disentanglement measurement.
attributes.rationale: Individual vector cosine similarity is inadequate for comparing subspaces; principal angles capture the full geometric relationship between subspaces.

nodes.label: PiSSA: Principal Singular Values and Vectors Adaptation

attributes.key_contribution: Initializes LoRA with principal singular components of pre-trained weights. Outperforms standard LoRA across 12 models, 13 tasks. Operational complement of TRS.

nodes.label: LoRA vs Full Fine-tuning: Intruder Dimensions (Shuttleworth et al.)

attributes.key_contribution: Introduces intruder dimensions: high-magnitude SVs in LoRA DISSIMILAR to pre-trained SVs. Suppressing them largely restores base model knowledge.

nodes.label: Small Singular Values Matter: RMT Analysis of Transformer Models (Staats et al.)

attributes.key_contribution: Uses MP as null; finds deviations at BOTH top AND bottom of spectrum are task-relevant. Removing small (near-zero) SVs post-fine-tuning causes outsized performance collapse.

nodes.label: Universal Weight Subspace Hypothesis

attributes.key_contribution: Analyzes 1,100+ models (500 Mistral-7B LoRAs, 500 ViTs, 50 LLaMA-8B). Diverse tasks concentrate weight updates in SHARED low-dimensional spectral subspaces. Directly corroborates TRS universality.

nodes.label: Learning in the Fisher Subspace: Guided Initialization for LoRA

attributes.key_contribution: Uses Fisher information matrix to identify task-relevant directions for LoRA initialization. Bridges Fisher geometry and LoRA singular value spectrum directly.

nodes.label: LoRA Training in the NTK Regime Has No Spurious Local Minima

attributes.key_contribution: Proves full fine-tuning admits low-rank solution of rank ~sqrt(N). LoRA with rank > sqrt(N) eliminates all spurious local minima. First formal guarantee that LoRA's restricted movement is sufficient.

nodes.label: Geometry of Neural Net Parameter Spaces Under Reparametrization (Kristiadi et al.)

attributes.key_contribution: Proves Fisher information metric is 'always present' and cannot be removed. Euclidean Hessian measures of flatness are coordinate-dependent. Riemannian foundation for why singular directions are geometrically privileged.

nodes.label: Physics-Inspired Singular Learning Theory to Understand Grokking

attributes.key_contribution: Applies Watanabe's RLCT to predict phase transitions. SLT implies MP bulk = degenerate (uninformative) singular model. Transitions ABOVE bulk signal change in geometric complexity.

nodes.label: Compressibility Measures Complexity: MDL Meets SLT

attributes.key_contribution: MDL principle to singular models via SLT. LLC (local learning coefficient) = geometric invariant of loss landscape. Linearly correlated with compressibility across quantization and factorization.

nodes.label: Bilinear MLPs Enable Weight-Based Mechanistic Interpretability

attributes.key_contribution: Bilinear MLPs expressible as linear operations via third-order tensor. Eigendecomposition of weights → interpretable low-rank structure. Recover circuits directly from weight matrices.

nodes.label: Interpretability in Parameter Space: APD (Attribution-based Parameter Decomposition)

attributes.key_contribution: Decomposes network weights into mechanistic components. Faithful, minimal, maximally simple decomposition. Parameters-first approach bridging MDL and mechanistic interpretability.

nodes.label: Revisiting Model Stitching to Compare Neural Representations (Bansal et al.)

attributes.key_contribution: Model stitching as stronger probe than CKA. Operational meaning: whether one model's geometry is usable by another. TRS cross-architecture universality can be tested via stitching.

nodes.label: Linear Mode Connectivity and the Lottery Ticket Hypothesis

attributes.key_contribution: Winning tickets = stable to SGD noise in weight space. Connects LMC geometry to subnetwork trainability.

nodes.label: Approaching Deep Learning through the Spectral Dynamics of Weights

attributes.key_contribution: Tracks SVD of weight matrices throughout training. Unifies grokking, lottery tickets, loss surface structure via spectral evolution. Weight decay acts geometrically to sharpen spectral structure.

nodes.label: The Spectral Lifecycle of Transformer Training

attributes.key_contribution: Tracks full SVD every 25 steps, 30M-285M param models. Discovers transient compression waves propagating depth-wise. Q/K asymmetry vs V in spectral terms. Rank and spectral shape encode fundamentally different training information.

nodes.label: No Task Left Behind: Isotropic Model Merging

attributes.key_contribution: Subspace Alignment Ratio from top SVD singular vectors. Grassmannian of leading singular subspaces as natural metric space for comparing models.

Winning tickets are stable to SGD noise in weight space and exhibit linear mode connectivity; this is consistent with lottery tickets lying on the same fiber (same TRS projection) as the fully trained model.

Both are above-MP singular vectors but distinguished by alignment with pre-trained SVs. True TRS predicts task performance; intruder dimensions predict catastrophic forgetting. Semantically opposite despite spectral similarity.

Both are markers of catastrophic forgetting: intruder dimensions cause forgetting by displacing pre-trained directions; near-zero SVs record what was suppressed. They describe forgetting from complementary perspectives.

Spectral-aware regularization in mtLoRA orthogonalizes low-SV (task-specific) components between tasks; this would reduce the development of intruder dimensions by preventing LoRA matrices from developing task-conflicting high-SV components.
Subspace boosting directly addresses rank collapse; they are two sides of the same phenomenon (problem and solution). The beta threshold in boosting is set to counteract the O(1/sqrt(N)) decay.

HO-GSVD decomposes N task vectors into individual U_i Sigma_i and shared V subspace; spectral-population duality claims population PCA = linear combination of individual TRS vectors. Both formalize how individual and population spectral structure relate.

hyperedges.label: Four-Way Spectral Decomposition Framework
hyperedges.description: Complete framework describing the four functionally distinct regions of the LoRA singular value spectrum and their roles in task adaptation, forgetting, and capability suppression.
hyperedges.rationale: The four-way decomposition is the central theoretical contribution of this synthesis session, combining insights from Shuttleworth (intruder dims), Staats (near-zero SVs), and the MP literature into a unified framework.

hyperedges.label: Spectral-Population Duality: TRS and Population PCA
hyperedges.description: The proposed equivalence between individual-model TRS vectors and population-level PCA principal components, unifying single-model spectral analysis with population-level weight space learning.
hyperedges.rationale: This duality is a theoretical prediction (not yet validated) connecting the single-model spectral view (TRS) with population-level methods (SANE, HO-GSVD). All participating nodes contribute to or would be explained by this framework.

hyperedges.label: Fiber Bundle Geometric Framework for Weight Space
hyperedges.description: The fiber bundle framework unifying weight space geometry: TRS as base space projection, G-symmetry as fiber structure, Fisher metric as connection, holonomy as task interference. Explains model composition, alignment difficulty, and mode connectivity as geometric phenomena.
hyperedges.rationale: The fiber bundle is the geometric unification framework proposed in the synthesis. All participating nodes are either components of the framework (holonomy, Grassmannian, TRS as base space) or provide theoretical grounding (Fisher geometry papers).
